Designing and building, as sole developer, a centralized headless CMS that replaces 8 separate Heroku and Strapi instances, targeting at least a 40% cut in monthly infrastructure cost.

A headless CMS that centralizes content management for every Novanet Studio web project. Each project gets an instantly available content API behind its own API key, replacing a fragmented setup of one Heroku and Strapi instance per client.
Multi-project architecture: projects hold collections and sub-collections nested to any depth, each isolated behind its own API key
Endpoint kill switch designed to take effect in under 2 seconds, checked against the database on every request
Visual field builder with 6 field types and global backups targeting under 3 minutes, with no DDL migrations or downtime

This project is part of an **ongoing freelance engagement with Novanet Studio** (since November 2024). Novanet Studio runs **a dedicated Heroku and Strapi instance for every web project**, which fragments maintenance and adds infrastructure cost with each new client. Kairos CMS replaces that model with **a single centralized instance**: once content is published, it becomes instantly available behind its own URL and API key, with no extra technical work. The pilot covers the studio's **8 active client projects**, and the roadmap opens the platform to external clients in V2.

The entire project, from *requirements and architecture to backend, frontend, QA and deployment*, is delivered by **a single developer** with no dedicated DevOps support. The hard constraints: **PaaS native with no Docker** at any phase, **no Redis** (Neon's serverless Postgres absorbs all read load by design), all media handled by Cloudinary so that **the backend never receives or stores a binary**, and collection schemas that stay **editable at any time without DDL migrations**. Older records remain accessible and are simply flagged as *out of format*. Clerk Auth and granular roles are deliberately deferred to V2.

A strict **4-layer architecture** keeps the core decoupled: Nuxt 4 for presentation, Express 5 for application logic, Drizzle ORM for data access and PostgreSQL 16 on Neon for persistence. Content is modeled as projects that hold collections, each bound to a **unique, irrevocable API key**, with sub-collections nested to any depth. Schemas persist as **JSONB instead of relational tables**, so the visual field builder can evolve them with **zero DDL migrations** while older records are preserved and flagged as *out of format*. The **endpoint kill switch** reads each collection's state from the database on every request, deliberately uncached, so a change takes effect in **under 2 seconds on every dyno**. Media travels **straight from the frontend to Cloudinary**, keeping the backend stateless. **Global backups run in a worker thread** that never blocks the event loop, and MVP auth is a self-hosted **JWT and bcrypt** session that defers Clerk's roles model to V2.

End-to-end modernization of Maximiza Casa de Bolsa's web presence. A rebuilt Nuxt 4 public site with an SEO and PWA overhaul, plus a new internal backoffice whose CRM captures and monitors every lead flowing in from the onboarding wizard, all backed by a NestJS + Neon Postgres platform.
Public site rebuilt on Nuxt 4 SSR with a full SEO overhaul: server-rendered pages, sitemap, robots and structured metadata
New internal backoffice (Nuxt 4 SPA) with a CRM module that tracks onboarding leads in real time over Socket.IO
Multichannel chatbot driven by a finite-state machine, sharing the same NestJS + Drizzle + Neon backend as the CRM

**Maximiza Casa de Bolsa** is a brokerage whose web presence ran on an aging stack that limited its SEO reach and gave the business **no visibility into the leads** generated by its own site. The project covers a full modernization: rebuild the public site on a current framework, fix the SEO foundation, and give the team an **internal backoffice with a CRM** to capture and monitor every prospect who starts the multistep onboarding form or reaches out over **WhatsApp**.

The public site and the admin panel are **separate Nuxt 4 apps** (SSR for SEO, SPA for the internal tool) talking to **a shared NestJS backend** on serverless Neon Postgres. Content (blog, financial balances) is served **over REST from Kairos CMS**, while all business logic, auth, and lead tracking live in the NestJS service. Sessions use a **JWT in an httpOnly cookie**, and lead updates must reach the CRM **live**, not on refresh.

The platform is split into **three apps around one backend**. The public site is **Nuxt 4 SSR** with a rebuilt SEO layer (sitemap, robots, structured metadata) and a **PWA**; its **multistep onboarding form** posts each step to the backend so no lead is lost mid-flow. The internal **backoffice is a Nuxt 4 SPA** (@nuxt/ui + Pinia) whose **CRM module** lists, assigns, and monitors those leads, with **ApexCharts** dashboards and **live updates over Socket.IO**. The backend is **NestJS 11 + Drizzle ORM on Neon Postgres**, exposing a consistent response envelope and cookie-based JWT auth; it also runs a **multichannel chatbot** as a finite-state machine sharing the same data layer. Onboarding PDFs are generated in-process with Puppeteer.

**Maximiza Casa de Bolsa** es una casa de bolsa cuya presencia web corría sobre un stack antiguo que limitaba su alcance SEO y no le daba **ninguna visibilidad sobre los leads** generados por su propio sitio. El proyecto abarcó una modernización completa: reconstruir el sitio público sobre un framework actual, reparar la base del SEO y dotar al equipo de un **backoffice interno con CRM** para capturar y monitorear cada prospecto que inicia el formulario multistep de onboarding o se comunica vía **WhatsApp**.

El sitio público y el panel de administración son **apps Nuxt 4 separadas** (SSR para SEO, SPA para la herramienta interna) que hablan con **un backend NestJS compartido** sobre Neon Postgres serverless. El contenido (blog, balances financieros) se consume **vía REST desde Kairos CMS**, mientras la lógica de negocio, la autenticación y el tracking de leads viven en el servicio NestJS. La sesión usa un **JWT en cookie httpOnly**, y las actualizaciones de leads deben llegar al CRM **en vivo**, no al recargar.

La plataforma se divide en **tres apps alrededor de un backend**. El sitio público es **Nuxt 4 SSR** con una capa de SEO renovada (sitemap, robots, metadata estructurada) y **PWA**; su **formulario multistep de onboarding** envía cada paso al backend para que ningún lead se pierda a mitad del flujo. El **backoffice interno es una SPA Nuxt 4** (@nuxt/ui + Pinia) cuyo **módulo CRM** lista, asigna y monitorea esos leads, con dashboards de **ApexCharts** y **actualizaciones en vivo por Socket.IO**. El backend es **NestJS 11 + Drizzle ORM sobre Neon Postgres**, con un envelope de respuesta consistente y auth JWT por cookie; además corre un **chatbot multicanal** como máquina de estados finitos sobre la misma capa de datos. Los PDFs de onboarding se generan in-process con Puppeteer.
